questions.q: Does adding an Ingress in front of order-api replace the order-api Service from Lesson 29?
options: No -- the Ingress routes external traffic to the same Service, which still does the actual pod selection
Yes -- Ingress objects replace Services entirely once created
Yes, but only for ClusterIP-type Services specifically
No -- Ingress objects route traffic directly to pods, bypassing Services completely
questions.explain: An Ingress sits in front of a Service and routes by host/path; it never replaces the Service's own pod selection.

questions.q: What does storageClassName: standard-rwo on the order-worker-data PVC actually trigger?
options: Nothing, unless a PersistentVolume is already pre-created by hand
It requests dynamic provisioning -- the cluster's StorageClass automatically creates a backing PersistentVolume
It forces the worker to use local, non-persistent disk only
It deletes any existing data in /data before the pod starts
questions.explain: Naming a StorageClass requests dynamic provisioning, per Chapter 5 -- nobody manually pre-creates the PersistentVolume.

questions.q: What problem does moving the four objects into a Helm chart with values.yaml solve?
options: It makes kubectl apply unnecessary forever
It automatically scales replicas based on live traffic
It pulls hard-coded values like image tags and replica counts into one file instead of duplicating them across every manifest
It removes the need for container images entirely
questions.explain: Templating with values.yaml is exactly the Chapter 6 problem being solved: one set of manifests, values centralized in one file.

questions.q: How does helm install order-app-staging produce a smaller release than the main order-app release?
options: Staging releases are always capped at 1 replica automatically by Helm itself
It uses a separate chart written specifically for staging
--set flags and a values-staging.yaml file override the chart's defaults for that specific release, without editing the chart's templates
It is not actually possible to run two differently sized releases from one chart
questions.explain: --set and --values override a chart's defaults per release -- the same chart can produce a full-size and a smaller release.

questions.q: What would happen to files order-worker writes to /data if the PVC from this lesson did not exist?
options: They would be written to the worker's writable container layer and lost whenever that pod is rescheduled or replaced
They would automatically be backed up to the registry
Kubernetes would refuse to start the worker pod at all
They would be stored permanently regardless of whether a volume is mounted
questions.explain: Without a mounted PersistentVolumeClaim, writes land in the pod's disposable writable layer and disappear when that pod goes away.
